--- workspace/fetch.sh	
+++ workspace/fetch.sh	
@@ -0,0 +1,39 @@
+#!/bin/bash
+set -e
+
+API="https://api.github.com/repos/canada-ca/accelerators_accelerateurs-aws"
+
+fetch() {
+    local url="$1"
+    local outfile="$2"
+    local status
+    status=$(curl -s -L -o "$outfile" -w "%{http_code}" "$url")
+    if [ "$status" -ge 400 ]; then
+        echo "Retrying $url after 5s..."
+        sleep 5
+        status=$(curl -s -L -o "$outfile" -w "%{http_code}" "$url")
+    fi
+    echo "$status" > "${outfile}.status"
+}
+
+fetch "$API" /workspace/repo.json
+sleep 1
+fetch "$API/contents/" /workspace/root_contents.json
+sleep 1
+fetch "$API/contents/CONTRIBUTING.md" /workspace/contributing.json
+sleep 1
+fetch "$API/contents/.github/workflows" /workspace/workflows.json
+sleep 1
+fetch "$API/contents/.github/dependabot.yml" /workspace/dependabot_yml.json
+sleep 1
+fetch "$API/contents/.github/dependabot.yaml" /workspace/dependabot_yaml.json
+sleep 1
+fetch "$API/contents/renovate.json" /workspace/renovate.json
+sleep 1
+fetch "$API/contents/.renovaterc.json" /workspace/renovaterc.json
+sleep 1
+fetch "$API/commits" /workspace/commits.json
+sleep 1
+fetch "$API/issues?state=open" /workspace/issues.json
+sleep 1
+fetch "$API/actions/runs" /workspace/actions_runs.json

GC Accelerators (AWS)

AWS has developed a project called the AWS Secure Environment Accelerator (ASEA) with the goal to accelerate the GC’s Amazon Web Services (AWS) deployments. It can be found at: https://github.com/aws-samples/aws-secure-environment-accelerator and it has been open-sourced by AWS under the Apache-2.0 License.

The ASEA is a tool designed to help deploy and operate secure multi-account, multi-region AWS environments on an ongoing basis and it enables the GC’s Cloud First direction and support for the GC Digital Standards. Using automation, the ASEA reduces the amount of effort required to meet the 12 GC Cloud Guardrails to less than 3 days and also meets many of the Protected B, Medium Integrity, Medium Availability (PBMM) compliance requirements.

The users of this project will be Government of Canada employees deploying cloud-based workloads.

Accélérateurs GC (AWS)

AWS a développé un projet appelé AWS Secure Environment Accelerator (ASEA) dans le but d'accélérer les déploiements Amazon Web Services (AWS) du GC. Il peut être trouvé à l’adresse suivante: https://github.com/aws-samples/aws-secure-environment-accelerator et il a été open-sourcé par AWS sous la licence Apache-2.0.

L’ASEA est un outil conçu pour aider à déployer et à gérer des environnements AWS sécurisés multi-comptes et multi-régions sur une base continue. Il permet d’orienter vers la direction du GC par l’informatique en nuage d’abord et de prendre en charge les normes numériques du GC. Grâce à l'automatisation, l'ASEA réduit à moins de 3 jours le montant d'effort requis pour répondre aux 12 mesures de sécurité en nuage du GC et répond également à un grand nombre des exigences de conformité Protégé B, intégrité moyenne et disponibilité moyenne (PBMM).

Les utilisateurs de ce projet seront des employés du gouvernement du Canada qui déploieront des charges de travail en nuage.

Comment contribuer

8. GraphQL API could work without auth for some queries but let's stick with scraping.

Actually, the webfetch tool has limitations - it might not support all GitHub pages well. Let me try using curl to fetch HTML pages directly. I need to be careful to avoid rate limits but HTML scraping is less likely to be rate limited than API.

Wait, I already have the main repo page HTML from the webfetch tool. From that HTML I extracted:
- Tree items: CONTRIBUTING.md, LICENSE, README.md, SECURITY.md
- Default branch: master
- Last commit oid: de38c856c2e276983a3c1a79a83f197b6100efb3

I still need:
- primary_language

- last commit date
- issues count
- workflow files

Let me use curl to fetch additional pages. I'll also try to use the GitHub GraphQL API which has different rate limits, or just fetch raw HTML.

Actually, I can try the GitHub API with the FIREWORKS_API_KEY or OPENAI_API_KEY? No, those are for OpenAI/Fireworks, not GitHub.

Let me try fetching HTML pages with curl.

The API calls are consistently blocked by 403 rate limits because the IP is not authenticated. GitHub API limits unauthenticated requests to 60 per hour. We have already hit the limit. However, we can still use HTML scraping with curl for additional pages.

The grep for relative-time datetime didn't work. Let's look at the commits.html structure. Maybe it uses a different attribute or the HTML is from a different page structure. Let's check the title first.
I need to extract the latest commit date from the commits page. Let me use a different pattern to find the first commit timestamp.

The HTML structure might have changed; GitHub now uses React with embedded JSON data, so `<relative-time>` tags may not be present in raw HTML. I need to parse the embedded JSON from the commits HTML.

Let me extract the embedded JSON from the commits page. Also need to check the issues HTML and license HTML.

input.command:
python3 -c "
import re, json
with open('/workspace/commits.html','r',encoding='utf-8') as f:
    text = f.read()
matches = re.findall(r'<script type=\"application/json\" data-target=\"react-app\.embeddedData\">(.*?)</script>', text, re.DOTALL)
print('matches', len(matches))
if matches:
    with open('/workspace/commits_embedded.json','w') as out:
        out.write(matches[0])
    data = json.loads(matches[0])
    print('keys', list(data.keys()))
    payload = data.get('payload', {})
    print('payload keys', list(payload.keys())[:20])
"

GC Accelerators (AWS)

AWS has developed a project called the AWS Secure Environment Accelerator (ASEA) with the goal to accelerate the GC’s Amazon Web Services (AWS) deployments.
